question.problem:
Determine whether $v=[\begin{aligned}-2\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}].$
If so, then what is the corresponding eigenvalue?
question.worked_solution:
The eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $v$ such that $Av=\lambda v.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4-8\text{i} \\ 4-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4{\text{i}}^{2}-8\text{i} \\ 4-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2\text{i}(4-2\text{i}) \\ 1(4-2\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =(4-2\text{i})[\begin{aligned}-2\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =(4-2\text{i})v.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $Av=(4-2\text{i})v,$ we conclude that $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ and the corresponding eigenvalue is $\lambda =4-2\text{i}.$
